results.result: The essential functional regions of LINE-1 and OR4K15 ribozymes consist of 35 and 31 nucleotides respectively, making them the simplest known self-cleaving ribozymes. These minimal core constructs (LINE-1-core and OR4K15-core) retain full catalytic activity.
results.evaluation: Claims C2, C46, C47, and C116 are directly supported by deep mutational scanning data (Figures 1B, 1C) showing that only two short segments in each ribozyme are sensitive to mutations. The claim that these are the simplest known self-cleaving ribozymes (C3, C116, C191, C192) is supported by comparison with other minimal ribozymes (≥36 nt for hammerhead and HDV-like). Functional validation is provided by cleavage assays (Figure 5B) demonstrating that the core constructs without stem-loop regions retain activity (C115, C193).

results.result: LINE-1-rbz and OR4K15-rbz are circular permutations of each other with nearly identical catalytic internal loops (L1), two stems (P1, P2), and a stem-loop region (SL2). The secondary structures were determined through deep mutational scanning and CODA analysis.
results.evaluation: The circular permutation relationship is well-supported by structural analysis (Figure 3A) and mutational data showing consistent effects for corresponding mutations (C164: U38C in LINE-1 has RA'=0.6, C8U in OR4K15 has RA=1.54). The secondary structure determination is validated by consistency between two independent rounds of deep mutational scanning (C162, C163) with high mutation coverage (99.3% single, 99.9% double mutations, C57). CODA analysis clearly identifies the two stems and internal loops (C63, C64, Figure 2B-D).

results.result: TS-like ribozymes share high sequence and secondary structure similarity with twister sister ribozymes, differing by only 1-2 bases in the catalytic internal loops. Pattern-based searches confirm this relationship.
results.evaluation: The similarity is well-documented through multiple lines of evidence: RNAbob pattern search yielding three hits all from twister sister class (C79), sequence comparison showing only one base difference per loop from four-way junctional twister sister (C80, Figure 3A), and near-identity with the env-33 sequence from twister sister alignment (C176: only one mismatch in OR4K15-rbz, no mismatch in LINE-1-rbz). The conserved cleavage sites further support structural similarity (C168).

results.result: Mutational effects at the cleavage site differ between TS-like and twister sister ribozymes. The cytosine at the cleavage site (C10 in LINE-1, C40 in OR4K15) is highly sensitive to mutations in TS-like ribozymes but insensitive in twister sister ribozymes.
results.evaluation: The differential mutational sensitivity is clearly demonstrated by experimental data: C10 mutations in LINE-1 show RA' as low as 0.07 (C99) and partial/complete loss of activity (C100, Figure 4C), while corresponding C62 mutations in twister sister showed pronounced or only somewhat reduced activity (C98, C101). Similarly, A11U in LINE-1-core showed partial activity while A63U in twister sister showed complete loss (C102). These differences indicate structural/mechanistic distinctions between the ribozyme classes (C103, C104).

results.result: Homology models of TS-like ribozymes were built using twister sister structure as template, but the validity and stability of these models is uncertain due to lack of tertiary interactions with stem-loop SL2 and absence of Mg2+ during modeling.
results.evaluation: While homology models were constructed (C82, C83) and show plausible structural features (C84-C87), multiple claims acknowledge significant uncertainty: the models may not remain stable without SL2 tertiary interactions (C96, C111, C175), Mg2+ was not included during modeling despite being essential for structure and catalysis (C184, C185, C186), and catalytic contacts required for activity were not observed in the models (C182, C183). The authors appropriately express uncertainty about whether the models represent the true functional structure.

results.result: TS-like ribozymes employ the standard internal phosphoester transfer mechanism and require Mg2+ for both structure folding and catalysis. Cleavage is observed with Mg2+, Mn2+, Co2+, and Zn2+ but not with Ca2+, monovalent ions, or Co(NH3)6³⁺ alone.
results.evaluation: The cleavage mechanism is confirmed by 2'-deoxy substitution experiments showing no cleavage when the 2'-OH is absent (C118, Figure 5B). Mg2+ dependence is clearly demonstrated: cleavage occurs with Mg2+ but not without it even after 24h (C112, C113, Figure 5—figure supplement 1). The requirement for divalent cations in both folding and catalysis is shown by loss of activity with Co(NH3)6³⁺ alone (C119, Figure 5C). Metal ion specificity is well-characterized (C120, Figure 5D).

results.result: TS-like ribozymes show distinct metal ion preferences and kinetic properties. LINE-1-core has kobs ~0.05 min⁻¹ with Mg2+, while both ribozymes show equivalent or higher activity with Mn2+ than Mg2+. The stem-loop SL2 contributes minimally to activity.
results.evaluation: Kinetic measurements are well-documented: LINE-1-core kobs ~0.05 min⁻¹ (C125, Figure 5—figure supplement 4), LINE-1-rbz ~0.03 min⁻¹ (C126), confirming minimal SL2 contribution (C127). Metal ion preferences are clearly shown: LINE-1-core 57% cleaved with Mg2+, 74% with Mn2+ (C123); OR4K15-core 9% with Mg2+, 79% with Mn2+ (C124). Concentration-dependent kinetics show plateaus at >100 mM Mg2+ and 10 mM Mn2+ (C129, C130). The differential ion preferences between the two ribozymes (C131, C132) suggest structural differences (C133), though this remains speculative.

results.result: Bioinformatic searches identified 1154 LINE-1-rbz homologs (mostly in L1PA7-9 subfamilies) and 4 OR4K15-rbz homologs in the human genome. Most LINE-1 homologs appear inactive due to mutations, while some OR4K15 homologs retain activity. Similar patterns exist in primate genomes.
results.evaluation: The bioinformatic findings are well-documented: cmsearch identified 1154 LINE-1 and 4 OR4K15 homologs (C135), with LINE-1 homologs concentrated in three subfamilies (C140, Figure 6B). Genomic locations are characterized (C136-C139, Figure 6A). The widespread A12C substitution in LINE-1 homologs correlates with loss of activity (C141, RA'=0.03), and experimental validation shows most selected homologs lack activity (C142, C143, Figure 6E-F). Primate genome analysis shows 15/18 have >500 LINE-1 homologs but most have ≥3 mismatches (C144, C146), while all have ≥1 exact OR4K15 match (C147).

results.result: Deep mutational scanning combined with CODA analysis provides highly accurate inference of RNA base-pairing structures. The second round using chemically synthesized doped libraries achieved 99.3% single and 99.9% double mutation coverage, overcoming error-prone PCR biases.
results.evaluation: The methodological validation is strong: the second round achieved near-complete mutation coverage (C57: 99.3% single, 99.9% double) compared to only 18.5% double mutation coverage in the first round (C58). The doped library approach reduced positional and mutational biases compared to error-prone PCR (C60, Figure 1—figure supplements 1-4). RA' was validated as a good estimate of RA with Pearson correlation 0.66 and Spearman 0.769 (C61). The consistency between results from original and functional region sequences provides additional validation (C162).

results.result: Various speculative claims about evolutionary origins, functional mechanisms, therapeutic potential, and future applications of TS-like ribozymes.
results.evaluation: These claims are explicitly speculative or require future work. Claims about primitive origins (C7), evolutionary relationships (C32, C156, C158), and finding additional circular-permutated forms (C166) are reasonable inferences but lack direct evidence. Therapeutic applications (C194, C196) are speculative based on the minimal size. The need for future structural and mechanistic studies is acknowledged (C187, C190). While these speculations are scientifically reasonable, they represent hypotheses rather than demonstrated results.

results.result: The essential functional regions of LINE-1 and OR4K15 ribozymes consist of 35 and 31 nucleotides respectively, making them the simplest known self-cleaving ribozymes. This was determined through deep mutational scanning experiments that identified the minimal regions required for ribozyme activity.
results.evaluation: Reviewers explicitly affirm this finding, stating 'The minimized domains appear to be some of the smallest known self-cleaving ribozymes.' The editor notes the study 'uncovers a surprising link between two self-cleaving RNAs' and the evidence is described as 'convincing and based on extensive biochemical and bioinformatic analysis.'

results.result: LINE-1 and OR4K15 ribozymes are circular permutations of each other with nearly identical catalytic internal loops. Both ribozymes have two stems (P1, P2), two internal loops, and a stem-loop region, with the secondary structure of OR4K15-rbz being a circular-permutated version of LINE-1-rbz.
results.evaluation: Reviewers describe the 'discovery of the common motif' as 'important and exciting' and note that 'The experiments support the HTS findings and provide convincing evidence that the ribozymes are structurally related.' The circular permutation relationship is treated as a key finding without challenge.

results.result: LINE-1 and OR4K15 ribozymes are similar to twister sister ribozymes in terms of sequence and secondary structure. Pattern-based similarity search yielded hits from the twister sister ribozyme class, and the internal loop regions differ from twister sister catalytic loops by only one or two bases, suggesting they share the same origin.
results.evaluation: Reviewers affirm this connection, noting the ribozymes are 'structurally related to the core of the TS ribozyme, which has not been found in primates prior to this work.' The editor describes this as an 'important study' that 'uncovers a surprising link' between the ribozymes and establishes them as belonging to the same structural family.

results.result: Mutational effects on TS-like ribozymes differ from those on twister sister ribozymes at the cleavage site. While cytosines at cleavage sites in twister sister ribozymes are insensitive to mutations, the corresponding cytosine (C10) in LINE-1-rbz is highly sensitive to mutations, suggesting TS-like ribozymes may not adopt exactly the same structure and catalytic mechanism as twister sister ribozymes.
results.evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge this finding without challenge. The detailed mutational analysis comparing TS-like and twister sister ribozymes is part of the 'extensive biochemical and bioinformatic analysis' that reviewers describe as 'convincing.' The differences in mutational sensitivity are presented as evidence supporting the distinctiveness of the TS-like class.

results.result: Deep mutational scanning identified that LINE-1-ori ribozyme activity is only sensitive to mutations in two short segments (54–71 and 83–99), while OR4K15-ori is sensitive only in segments 70–84 and 101–116. This led to identification of contiguous functional regions LINE-1-rbz (54–99) and OR4K15-rbz (70–116), with terminal ends and central regions being dispensable for activity.
results.evaluation: Reviewers describe the manuscript as 'rooted in deep mutational analysis' and state that 'The experiments support the HTS findings.' The identification of functional regions through mutational scanning is treated as a foundational result that is well-supported by the data.

results.result: CODA analysis combined with Monte Carlo simulated annealing (CODA+MC) revealed the secondary structures of both ribozymes, identifying two stem regions in each. LINE-1-rbz has stems of 6 nt and 5 nt with a possible non-canonical A6A41 pair, while OR4K15-rbz has stems of 5 nt and 4 nt with a G14U33 wobble pair. The final structures contain two stem regions (P1, P2), two internal loops, and a stem-loop.
results.evaluation: Reviewers affirm the structural determination, noting the work provides 'convincing evidence' for the ribozyme structures. The CODA analysis methodology is implicitly accepted as the reviewers focus on the resulting structural insights rather than questioning the analytical approach.

results.result: A second round of deep mutational scanning using chemically synthesized doped libraries achieved 99.3% and 99.9% coverage of single and double mutations for LINE-1-rbz, compared to only 18.5% double mutation coverage in the first round. This technological improvement led to less biased mutations compared to error-prone PCR, with RA′ showing strong correlation (Pearson 0.66, Spearman 0.769) with RA from the original sequence.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge the methodological improvements or coverage statistics. The high mutation coverage is implicitly accepted as part of the 'extensive biochemical and bioinformatic analysis' that provides 'convincing evidence' for the main conclusions.

results.result: Homology modeling based on the four-way junctional twister sister ribozyme structure (PDB: 5Y87) revealed tertiary structure features of TS-like ribozymes. The models show stem extensions through base triples and non-canonical pairs, with U38 (LINE-1) or C8 (OR4K15) extruded from the helix. However, the stability of these models in the absence of tertiary interactions with stem-loop SL2 is uncertain.
results.evaluation: While reviewers accept the overall structural similarity to twister sister ribozymes, they do not explicitly validate the detailed homology modeling predictions. The authors themselves acknowledge uncertainty about model stability, stating 'it is not entirely clear whether the model structure...will remain stable.' This represents computational inference rather than direct experimental validation.

results.result: The validity and stability of the homology-modeled structures is uncertain. The models lack direct contacts stabilizing the scissile phosphate and in-line alignments required for catalysis, suggesting conformational changes may be required. The absence of Mg2+ during modeling and lack of tertiary interactions with SL2 may affect structural accuracy.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not explicitly address these uncertainties about the homology models. The authors themselves express multiple caveats about model validity, noting it is 'not entirely clear' whether structures will remain stable and that 'further studies are needed.' This represents acknowledged limitations rather than reviewer-identified concerns.

results.result: Biochemical validation experiments demonstrated that TS-like ribozymes cleave in trans in the presence of Mg2+, with no cleavage observed without Mg2+ even after 24 hours. The ribozymes employ the same internal phosphoester transfer mechanism as other self-cleaving ribozymes, confirmed by loss of activity with 2′-deoxy substitutions at the -1 nucleotide. The stem-loop SL2 regions do not participate in catalytic activity.
results.evaluation: Reviewers describe the biochemical experiments as providing 'convincing evidence' without raising concerns about the cleavage assays or mechanistic conclusions. The trans-cleavage activity and Mg2+ dependence are treated as well-established findings supporting the ribozyme characterization.

results.result: Metal ion specificity experiments showed that TS-like ribozymes require divalent cations for both folding and catalysis. At 1 mM concentration, cleavage occurs with Mg2+, Mn2+, Co2+, and Zn2+ but not with Ca2+, Cu2+, Ba2+, Ni2+, or monovalent ions. Interestingly, TS-like ribozymes show equivalent or higher cleavage with Mn2+ than Mg2+ (LINE-1: 57% vs 74%; OR4K15: 9% vs 79%).
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge the metal ion dependence data. These experiments are part of the 'extensive biochemical' analysis that reviewers describe as convincing. The metal specificity results support the characterization of the ribozymes' catalytic requirements.

results.result: Kinetic characterization showed LINE-1-core has kobs ~0.05 min⁻¹ in 10 mM MgCl2, while LINE-1-rbz has slightly lower kobs ~0.03 min⁻¹, confirming SL2 contributes little to activity. Rate constants plateau at >100 mM Mg2+ or 10 mM Mn2+. LINE-1-core shows higher cleavage rates than OR4K15-core with Mg2+, but OR4K15-core is higher with Mn2+ at concentrations >20 mM.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not question the kinetic measurements. These data are part of the biochemical characterization that reviewers describe as 'extensive' and 'convincing.' The kinetic differences between the two ribozymes and metal ion preferences are accepted as reported.

results.result: Bioinformatic searches identified 1154 LINE-1-rbz homologs and 4 OR4K15-rbz homologs in the human genome. There is an exact match for OR4K15-rbz in the OR4K15 gene and three homologs in the same olfactory receptor subfamily, but no exact match for LINE-1-rbz. Most LINE-1 homologs map to three subfamilies (L1PA7, L1PA8, L1P3) and contain an A12C substitution that extends stem P2 but abolishes activity. In vitro assays showed most homologs lack significant cleavage activity.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge the bioinformatic analysis or the finding that most genomic homologs appear inactive. This genomic distribution analysis is part of the overall study that reviewers describe as providing 'convincing evidence' through 'extensive...bioinformatic analysis.'

results.result: Analysis of primate genomes showed 15 of 18 have >500 LINE-1 homologs while three have essentially none. Most LINE-1-rbz homologs in primates have three or more mismatches and appear inactive, except for one Gibbon homolog with a single U38C mutation. All representative primate genomes contain at least one exact match of OR4K15-rbz sequence.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not question the primate genome analysis. The finding that TS-like ribozymes 'have not been found in primates prior to this work' is explicitly noted by reviewers as significant, implicitly accepting the genomic distribution data.

results.result: The maximum kobs for TS-like ribozymes (~0.11 ± 0.01 min⁻¹) is ~45-fold slower than twister sister ribozyme (~5 min⁻¹). This rate difference is not mainly caused by mismatches in the catalytic core, as individual mismatches show only moderate activity reduction. Instead, the more sophisticated structure with long-range interactions involving the SL4 region in twister sister ribozyme helps stabilize the catalytic region for improved activity.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge the kinetic comparison with twister sister ribozymes or the interpretation about structural contributions to catalytic efficiency. This analysis is part of the comparative characterization that reviewers find convincing.

results.result: The OR4K15 ribozyme is located at the reverse strand of the coding region of the OR4K15 gene, suggesting a potentially novel functional mechanism involving antisense transcription. Unlike the conserved CPEB3 ribozyme with clear function, TS-like ribozymes are not conserved, belong to pseudogenes, or are on the reverse strand, making their function unclear.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge the genomic location findings or the speculation about novel functional mechanisms. The unusual genomic context is implicitly accepted as part of the 'detailed analysis' that reviewers describe, though the functional implications remain speculative.

results.result: The location of LINE-1 ribozyme in the 5′ UTR suggests it might be related to transcriptional regulation of LINE-1 retrotransposon during evolution, similar to HDV-like ribozymes. The self-cleavage activity may share a common evolutionary path with retrotransposition activity, as most LINE-1 elements are now inactive 'DNA fossils.'
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not explicitly evaluate these evolutionary and functional speculations. The authors present these as inferences based on genomic location and comparison with other ribozyme systems, but they remain hypothetical without direct functional validation. Reviewers focus on the structural characterization rather than evolutionary implications.

results.result: TS-like ribozymes have the simplest secondary structure (two stems and two internal loops) compared to all naturally occurring self-cleaving ribozymes. The conserved segments (31 nt) are shorter than minimized hammerhead and HDV-like ribozymes (≥36 nt). The minimal trans-cleaving form requires only 15-nt enzyme and 16-nt substrate strands, potentially offering advantages for bioengineering and RNA-targeting therapeutics.
results.evaluation: Reviewers explicitly affirm this finding, stating 'The minimized domains appear to be some of the smallest known self-cleaving ribozymes.' The potential therapeutic applications are speculative but reviewers do not challenge the structural simplicity claims or size comparisons.

results.result: This work confirms the usefulness of deep mutational scanning combined with high-throughput sequencing for RNA structural inference by CODA analysis. The method successfully led to highly accurate inference of base-pairing structures for the TS-like ribozymes.
results.evaluation: Reviewers affirm the methodological contribution, noting the manuscript is 'rooted in deep mutational analysis' and that 'The experiments support the HTS findings and provide convincing evidence.' The successful application of CODA analysis to determine ribozyme structures is treated as a validated methodological approach.

results.result: Self-cleaving ribozymes in the human genome are few and poorly studied, with little known about human ribozymes other than CPEB3. Progress in understanding LINE-1 and OR4K15 ribozymes was slow due to lacking structural clues prior to this study.
results.evaluation: Reviewers implicitly accept this characterization of the field, noting 'Very few human/primate ribozymes have been published and this manuscript presents a detailed analysis of two of them.' The study is described as 'important' precisely because it addresses this knowledge gap.

comparisons.comparison: Strong agreement on differential mutational sensitivity between TS-like and twister sister ribozymes (C6, C98-C104, C179-C180). Both evaluations find the evidence convincing and well-supported by experimental data showing distinct mutation effects at corresponding positions.

Strong agreement on structural similarity to twister sister ribozymes (C5, C79-C80, C167, C176-C177). Both evaluations affirm the connection through sequence comparison and RNAbob pattern search, treating this as a key finding without challenge.

Strong agreement on methodological validation (C57-C58, C60-C61). Both evaluations accept the high mutation coverage and improved methodology. OpenEval provides detailed validation metrics while peer reviewers implicitly accept these as part of 'extensive biochemical analysis.'

Strong agreement on kinetic measurements (C125-C132). Both evaluations support the reported kinetic data, metal ion preferences, and concentration-dependent effects. Peer reviewers describe this as part of 'convincing' biochemical characterization.

Both evaluations express uncertainty about homology models (C82-C95). OpenEval explicitly categorizes as UNCERTAIN citing lack of Mg2+ and missing catalytic contacts. Peer reviewers do not explicitly validate detailed modeling predictions, acknowledging computational inference limitations.

Strong agreement on cleavage mechanism and Mg2+ dependence (C112-C115, C118). Both evaluations find the 2'-deoxy substitution and metal ion experiments convincing. Peer reviewers describe biochemical evidence as 'convincing' without raising concerns.

Strong agreement on bioinformatic findings (C135-C143). Both evaluations support the genomic distribution analysis, identification of homologs, and finding that most genomic copies appear inactive due to mutations like A12C.

Strong agreement on circular permutation relationship (C4, C72-C73, C76-C77). Both evaluations find this 'important and exciting' discovery well-supported by structural analysis and mutational data. OpenEval provides more detailed validation through mutation correspondence.

Strong agreement on minimal ribozyme size (C2-C3, C116). Both evaluations affirm these are among the smallest known self-cleaving ribozymes. Peer reviewers explicitly state 'The minimized domains appear to be some of the smallest known self-cleaving ribozymes.'

Both evaluations express uncertainty about homology model validity (C96, C111, C175, C182-C184, C186). OpenEval categorizes as UNCERTAIN; peer reviewers do not explicitly address but authors acknowledge limitations about model stability and missing Mg2+.

Strong agreement on methodological contribution (C38, C197). Both evaluations affirm the successful application of deep mutational scanning and CODA analysis. Peer reviewers note manuscript is 'rooted in deep mutational analysis' providing 'convincing evidence.'

Strong agreement on minimal size and simplicity (C191-C193). Both evaluations support claims about these being among the smallest ribozymes. OpenEval includes functional validation data; peer reviewers explicitly affirm the size comparison.

Strong agreement on primate genome analysis (C144-C147, C155). Both evaluations accept the finding that TS-like ribozymes were not previously found in primates and the genomic distribution data across 18 primate genomes.

Strong agreement on metal ion dependence (C119-C121). Both evaluations support the divalent cation requirements and metal specificity data. Peer reviewers treat this as part of 'extensive biochemical' analysis without challenge.

Both evaluations express uncertainty about evolutionary speculations (C32, C156, C158). OpenEval categorizes as UNCERTAIN noting these are reasonable inferences lacking direct evidence. Peer reviewers do not explicitly evaluate these hypothetical claims.

Partial overlap on metal ion characterization (C122-C124). OpenEval covers broader kinetic analysis while peer review focuses on metal dependence. Both find the metal ion preference data convincing and well-supported.

Partial overlap on functional regions (C46-C47). OpenEval focuses on minimal ribozyme claims with deep mutational scanning support. Peer reviewers affirm the mutational analysis methodology identifying functional regions.

Partial overlap on therapeutic applications (C194, C196). OpenEval categorizes these as speculative claims requiring future work. Peer reviewers do not challenge the speculation but focus on affirming the structural simplicity that motivates it.

Minimal overlap on kinetic comparisons (C169). OpenEval includes this in broader kinetic analysis. Peer reviewers accept the twister sister comparison without challenge as part of overall characterization.

Minimal overlap on secondary structure (C71). OpenEval focuses on circular permutation validation. Peer review R6 addresses CODA analysis and structural determination more broadly, both finding evidence convincing.

Peer review R5 addresses functional region identification through mutational scanning (C42-C47, C62-C64) as foundational results. OpenEval addresses these claims within R1 (minimal ribozyme structure) rather than as separate evaluation.

Peer review R6 addresses CODA analysis and secondary structure determination (C48-C71) as distinct evaluation. OpenEval incorporates these methodological claims within R2 (circular permutation) and R9 (methodological validation).

Peer review R16 addresses genomic location findings (C37, C159, C189) and speculation about novel functional mechanisms. OpenEval includes C32 in R10 (speculative claims) but does not separately evaluate genomic context claims.

Peer review R20 addresses characterization of the field and knowledge gap (C1, C21, C160). OpenEval does not separately evaluate these contextual/background claims about the state of ribozyme research.

OpenEval R10 groups multiple speculative claims (C7, C32, C156, C158, C166, C173, C175, C183, C187, C190, C194, C196, C198-C199) as UNCERTAIN requiring future work. Peer reviewers address subsets separately (R17, R18) or do not explicitly evaluate.
